standard.title: SPECIFICATION FOR POWER TRANSMISSION — BELTS, ENDLESS FLAT (USED IN LENIX DRIVE SYSTEM)
standard.sector: Pulleys and Belts Sectional Committee, LMD 09
standard.description: This standard covers the requirements of endless cord lenix flat belts for the use of power transmission in jute machineries like spinning frames, carding machines, drawing frames and softener machines, etc. These belts are also used for machine tools, compressors and pumps. These belts are generally used for fixed centre drives where idler pulleys are utilised for belt tension adjustments, and can also be used for drives where adjustment of centres is available.
standard.scope: This standard covers the requirements of endless cord lenix flat belts for the use of power transmission in jute machineries like spinning frames, carding machines, drawing frames and softener machines, etc. These belts are also used for machine tools, compressors and pumps. These belts are generally used for fixed centre drives where idler pulleys are utilised for belt tension adjustments, and can also be used for drives where adjustment of centres is available.

certification.description: Supported by the Bureau of Indian Standards Certification Marking scheme, providing assurance of quality control and manufacturing compliance under the statutory provisions of the BIS.
requirements: Specifies flat endless type belts with round edges manufactured in widths ranging from 25 mm to 300 mm and thickness from 3 mm to 9.5 mm. The length of the belt must indicate the inside circumference only.
The tension member must consist of cable cord or weftless woven cords. Depending upon the required power rating, the number of layers of the tension member varies from 1 to 6 layers.

The body consists of two or more layers of rubberised fabric incorporating the cords. The enveloping rubberised fabric is bias cut for joining. The joint must be covered with a thin rubberised fabric breaker strip to strengthen the joint and maintain a uniform belt thickness.
Enforces a strict nominal hardness of 90° ± 5° (Durometer A). Hardness variations beyond ± 5° significantly impair belt flexibility and drive performance.

When tested using a 25 mm wide belt with 180 mm jaw separation and reference marks 100 mm apart under specified load, the maximum permissible elongation is limited to 2.5% across all thicknesses: 120 N for 3 mm; 200 N for 5 mm; 300 N for 6.4 mm; and 400 N for 9.5 mm.
Each belt thickness must withstand a specified minimum rupture force: 1200 N for 3 mm; 2000 N for 5 mm; 4000 N for 6.4 mm; and 10200 N for 9.5 mm.
The adhesion between different layers of fabric to cord must be a minimum of 22 N per 10 mm width when tested in accordance with Annex C of IS : 1370 - 1979.

For mechanical testing (breaking strength and elongation), test pieces of 25 mm width and not less than 300 mm length must be cut containing no joints, cut not less than 5 days from manufacture, and conditioned for 3 days at 27 ± 2°C and 65 ± 5% relative humidity.
